votes.reason: Cheap and sound: 16.4x trailing earnings on EPS up 13.4%, with the lowest weekly volatility on the sheet (1.57%), and even after its 15.0% twelve-week run it is still the second-cheapest name here.

UNH costs 21.1x trailing earnings that fell 26.1% against the prior four quarters, a richer multiple than JPM or PGR on the sharpest earnings decline on the sheet, so it fails both halves of my test and looks like a value trap rather than a bargain to hold at a 20% weight.
The cheapest name on the sheet at 11.6x trailing earnings with EPS still up 10.1%, a sound and growing underwriter at a real discount.

At 21.8x trailing earnings with EPS roughly flat (-3.9%), a dominant, highly profitable business is fairly priced rather than stretched, and the settlement swaps an open-ended legal risk for a known cost; its 6.63% weekly volatility is a sizing matter the draft already handles at 15%.

PM carries the richest multiple on the sheet (23.7x trailing) near its 52-week high, so its margin of safety comes from 14.7% EPS growth and 2.37% weekly volatility rather than from the price, which is sound enough for its role as the Staples hedge.
